L14·N4051unmasked layer
This neuron is essentially a sentence-continuation vs. boundary detector: it fires on ordinary mid-sentence tokens that continue an unfinished phrase (e.g. "of", "to", "The", the second half of a compound noun like "rice powder", or a rare word like "kratom"), and is strongly suppressed on paragraph/line-break "\n" tokens and trailing ellipses that end a segment.

L15·N5865unmasked layer
This neuron fires on the token that begins a predicate/definition right after a named subject — chiefly copulas (" is", " are") or a definitional colon following a noun phrase (e.g. "Rainbows are…", "Cream is…", "the new york public library:"), while being suppressed on continuations of proper-noun/compound names ("Grand Canyon", "Pitchfork", "leg-ume").
